([[Minnetonka, Minnesota]]) | college = [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2019–20 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2020]]) * All-Freshman team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2019–20 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2020]]) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]] (2020) | medal_templates = }} '''Ezekiel Tobechukwu "Zeke" Nnaji''' (born January 9, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==Early life== Nnaji played [[baseball]] and [[soccer]] before starting [[basketball]] due to his height. He has played the [[piano]] since first grade. Nnaji composes his own music.{{cite web |last1=Max |first1=Mike |title=Top High School Basketball Player Doubles As Concert Pianist |url=https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2018/12/28/high-school-basketball-player-concert-pianist-zeke-nnaji/ |website=[[WCCO-TV]] |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |date=December 28, 2018}} ==High school career== Nnaji started playing high school basketball for [[Lakeville North High School]] in [[Lakeville, Minnesota]], before transferring to [[Hopkins High School]] in [[Minnetonka, Minnesota]]. As a senior, he averaged 24.1 points and 9.4 rebounds per game and led Hopkins to a Minnesota 4A state title over Lakeville North.{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Minnesota's Zeke Nnaji is third Arizona Wildcats recruit to win state title |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/minnesota-s-zeke-nnaji-is-third-arizona-wildcats-recruit-to/article_5df07b46-4df3-11e9-a50e-afe4036fbf32.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |accessdate=November 26, 2019 |date=March 23, 2019}} Nnaji had 14 points and 12 rebounds in the championship game. He played for the Adidas-sponsored D1 Minnesota club alongside [[Matthew Hurt]]. Nnaji was invited to the Iverson Classic game. Nnaji was ranked 22nd in his class and a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] but was considered a four-star recruit by most other recruiting services.{{cite news |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=How Arizona's Zeke Nnaji slipped under the radar and became one of college basketball's early-season stars |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/how-arizona-s-zeke-nnaji-slipped-under-the-radar-and/article_a641c444-2694-5ff1-91e9-56966fbaa4c8.html |accessdate=November 30, 2019 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=November 20, 2019}} He committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].{{cite web |last1=Geary |first1=Molly |title=Arizona Moves to No. 1 in 2019 Recruiting Class Rankings With Commitment of Zeke Nnaji |url=https://www.si.com/college/2018/11/23/arizona-basketball-recruiting-sean-miller-zeke-nnaji |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |date=November 23, 2018}} ==College career== On November 6, 2019, Nnaji made his college debut, scoring 20 points in 21 minutes to help Arizona defeat [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona]], 91–52.{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Freshman Zeke Nnaji's special debut calls to mind memories of D-Will, other Wildcats standouts |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/freshman-zeke-nnaji-s-special-debut-calls-to-mind-memories/article_c1067987-1a5f-5ce4-b825-bf5f5b3467d7.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |date=November 7, 2019}} Five days later, he was named [[Pac-12 Conference]] Freshman of the Week.{{cite web |last1=Scheer |first1=Jason |title=Zeke Nnaji named Pac-12 Freshman of the Week |url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona/Article/Zeke-Nnaji-Pac-12-Freshman-of-the-Week-138449900/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |date=November 11, 2019}} Nnaji won the same award in the following week, most notably posting 26 points and 11 rebounds in an 87–39 win over [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]].{{cite web |last1=Pedersen |first1=Brian J. |title=Zeke Nnaji wins second straight Pac-12 Freshman of the Week award |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2019/11/18/20971319/zeke-nnaji-arizona-wildcats-pac12-freshman-award-weekly-basketball-2019 |website=Arizona Desert Swarm |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |date=November 18, 2019}} He became the first Arizona player to score 20 points and collect 10 rebounds in his in his first three games since [[Brandon Ashley]] did so against [[Long Beach State 49ers men's basketball|Long Beach State]] in the 2012–13 season.{{cite news |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Freshman Zeke Nnaji could help bust zones thrown at Arizona Wildcats basketball |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2019/11/16/arizona-wildcats-basketball-zeke-nnaji-could-help-bust-zones-ua/4218300002/ |accessdate=November 30, 2019 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=November 16, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Nnaji was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]].{{Cite web|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2020/03/08/2019-20-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards-announced|title=Pac-12 announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball annual major awards|date=March 9, 2020|website=pac-12.com|access-date=March 9, 2020}} Nnaji averaged 16.1 points per game on 57 percent shooting and grabbed 8.6 rebounds per game as a freshman. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Helin |first1=Kurt |title=Arizona’s Zeke Nnaji, DePaul’s Paul Reed declare for NBA draft |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/03/29/arizonas-zeke-nnaji-depauls-paul-reed-declare-for-nba-draft/ |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 29, 2020|accessdate=March 30, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] | 32 || 32 || 30.7 || .570 || .294 || .760 || 8.6 || .8 || .7 || .9 || 16.1 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Nnaji's father, Alphan, is from [[Nigeria]], while his mother, Janel, is from [[Minnesota]]. His younger sister, Maya, is a highly regarded high school basketball recruit at [[Hopkins High School]].{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Here's why Sean Miller says Zeke Nnaji, Arizona's bulked-up, piano-playing freshman, can do big things |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/here-s-why-sean-miller-says-zeke-nnaji-arizona-s/article_3e143706-c513-5337-9928-bc97150c9485.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |date=September 14, 2019}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://arizonawildcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/zeke-nnaji/10612 Arizona Wildcats bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/n/nnaji-zeke.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Nnaji, Zeke}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:American people of Nigerian descent]] [[Category:Arizona Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Minnesota]] [[Category:Hopkins High School alumni]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Minneapolis]]
